thread:
Maya: Quick sync — I'm drafting the preflight 'slice definitions' we want for GA. Need signoff on: SLA tiers, docs owner, oncall coverage, pricing guardrails, and test signal sets. Who can weigh in?
Tom: I can do SLA/pricing bits. propose: production slice = 99.9%  p95 latency < 150ms, burst queue < 200ms.
Elena: I'll own docs + prompt sets. Can we keep the public doc minimal and an internal runbook with the full checklist?
Chris: For oncall: recommend 24/7 paging for P0/P1, weekday pager for P2, and async on P3. Need to map owners for the dedicated vs hosted lanes.
Alex: Heads up — Dedicated customers will want a higher SLA; we should call out a separate contractable SLA and ops runway.
sre-bot: Incident template suggestion: /incident create ga_preflight_slice — includes fields: "service-tier", "slice-id", "observability-link".
Maya: Agree on two SLA tracks: Hosted (our default published SLA) and Dedicated (contract). Hosted baseline 99.9% with clear fallbacks (model-variant routing) if capacity constrained.
Tom: Pricing guardrail thought: soft limit per-customer token rate with an alerting threshold at 80% and auto-throttle at 95% to protect shared pools. Document as "quota escalation policy".
Elena: Docs owners: Elena -> public docs (short page + FAQ), Maya -> internal runbook (detailed acceptance test steps), Tom -> pricing section. I'll create the public stub today: https://go.redwood/docs/preflight-slices (WIP).
Chris: Monitoring: we need per-slice dashboards: error rate, tail latency, queue length, model-fallback count, cost per 1M tokens. Add synthetic smoke tests that run hourly.
Alex: For Dedicated, we should require a canary window and a contract clause for capacity reservation. Ops needs a playbook to escalate to infra within 15m for capacity alarms.
Maya: Ownership matrix (draft): Product: Maya (overall), Docs: Elena, Pricing & Quotas: Tom, Oncall routing: Chris, Dedicated contracts: Alex. Can everyone ack?
Tom: Ack from me. I'll prepare the pricing excerpt and a sample quota policy.
Elena: Ack. I'll drop the internal runbook template in #docs-ops and link it from the stub.
Chris: Ack. Will add oncall rotations and the pager thresholds to the runbook.
Alex: Ack. I'll write the dedicated SLA appendix and sample contract language.
Maya: Next steps: I'll assemble a one-pager for execs with the acceptance gates: 1) SLA simulator pass, 2) docs and runbook published, 3) oncall rota + playbook, 4) pricing/quota policy, 5) synthetic smoke green for 24h. Aim to have that by EOD Friday.
Tom: ETA: pricing draft by Thursday noon.
Elena: Docs stub live by Thursday EOD.
Chris: Paging + smoke tests in staging by Friday morning.
Alex: Dedicated appendix draft by Friday EOD.
Maya: Cool. If anyone hits blockers ping me or drop a short note here. Thanks :thumbsup:
